units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
Then why does he write to me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: What do you mean?
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What letter is this?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Takes up letter .
That—is nothing. Give it to me.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: It is addressed to me .
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You are not to open it. I forbid you to open it.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: And in Gerald’s handwriting.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It was not to have been sent. It is a letter he wrote to you this morning, before he saw me. But he is sorry now he wrote it, very sorry. You are not to open it. Give it to me.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: It belongs to me.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Opens it , sits down and reads it slowly .
MRS. ARBUTHNOT watches him all the time .
You have read this letter, I suppose, Rachel?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: No.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: You know what is in it?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Yes!
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I don’t admit for a moment that the boy is right in what he says. I don’t admit that it is any duty of mine to marry you. I deny it entirely. But to get my son back I am ready—yes, I am ready to marry you, Rachel—and to treat you always with the deference and respect due to my wife. I will marry you as soon as you choose. I give you my word of honour.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You made that promise to me once before and broke it.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I will keep it now. And that will show you that I love my son, at least as much as you love him. For when I marry you, Rachel, there are some ambitions I shall have to surrender. High ambitions, too, if any ambition is high.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I decline to marry you, Lord Illingworth.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Are you serious?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Yes.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Do tell me your reasons. They would interest me enormously.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I have already explained them to my son.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I suppose they were intensely sentimental, weren’t they? You women live by your emotions and for them. You have no philosophy of life.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You are right. We women live by our emotions and for them. By our passions, and for them, if you will. I have two passions, Lord Illingworth: my love of him, my hate of you. You cannot kill those. They feed each other.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What sort of love is that which needs to have hate as its brother?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It is the sort of love I have for Gerald. Do you think that terrible? Well it is terrible. All love is terrible. All love is a tragedy. I loved you once, Lord Illingworth. Oh, what a tragedy for a woman to have loved you!
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: So you really refuse to marry me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Yes.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Because you hate me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Yes.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: And does my son hate me as you do?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: No.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I am glad of that, Rachel.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: He merely despises you.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What a pity! What a pity for him, I mean.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Don’t be deceived, George. Children begin by loving their parents. After a time they judge them. Rarely if ever do they forgive them.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Reads letter over again , very slowly .
May I ask by what arguments you made the boy who wrote this letter, this beautiful, passionate letter, believe that you should not marry his father, the father of your own child?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It was not I who made him see it. It was another.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What fin-de-siècle person?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: The Puritan, Lord Illingworth.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: A pause .
Winces , then rises slowly and goes over to table where his hat and gloves are .
MRS. ARBUTHNOT is standing close to the table .
He picks up one of the gloves, and begins pulling it on .
There is not much then for me to do here, Rachel?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH
